papers.authors: Sabrina Grandclaude, Didier Grandclaude, Thierry Nobre, Cadenza Academic Translations
papers.summary: Based on the analysis of 96 organizational innovation in healthcare (OIH) projects and 52 interviews conducted with project leaders initiating these innovations, this research identifies the phenomena underlying the genesis of OIHs. The results highlight the major role played by factors such as patient empathy, international inspiration, academic inspiration, technological inspiration, serendipitous encounters, and the desire for organizational transformation in driving the generation of OIHs. Furthermore, our findings emphasize the dual nature of the research and development process for these innovations, characterized as both ex nihilo and ex materia.

papers.title: A collaborative and participatory approach to public service innovation: Health sector dynamics and outlook
papers.title_ja: 公共医療サービスにおける協働的・参加型革新へのアプローチ
papers.authors: Fatima Yatim, Alan Sitkin, Cadenza Academic Translations
papers.summary: This article explores the dynamics of collaborative and participatory innovations in public health services using Chen et al.’s (2020) typology. Based on a mixed survey of projects awarded under the national “Droits des usagers de la santé” initiative, the study finds that user participation primarily generates operational and capacity-oriented innovations frequently involving external partnerships. The analysis highlights the crucial interactions between internal and external dynamics, identifying essential conditions for successful innovations: effective mobilization of internal resources, robust institutional support, and early and active user involvement. However, the study also identifies limitations in citizen engagement, particularly in the evaluation phase of innovations. The article concludes by suggesting avenues for enhancing full co-creation processes in public services to maximize public value.

papers.summary: This exploratory research aims to characterize, on the one hand, the concept of environmental management control (EMC) through the practices that underpin it, and, on the other hand, the tensions associated with it and the implementation of these practices in public organizations. Although EMC is attracting growing interest within the public sector, it seems to be facing technical and governance difficulties. A grid for analyzing management tools and the theory of organizational paradoxes is used to address the issue of characterizing EMC practices and the associated tensions in the local public sector. Various municipalities were mobilized to explore and characterize their first experiences of implementing EMC. Our results enable us to characterize both the tools used and the tensions generated between the objectives pursued in terms of resource management, dialogue with the socio-economic environment, and behavioral orientation.

papers.summary: Here we investigate the effects of extensive sociality and mobility on the oral microbiome of 138 Agta hunter-gatherers from the Philippines. Our comparisons of microbiome composition showed that the Agta are more similar to Central African Bayaka hunter-gatherers than to neighbouring farmers. We also defined the Agta social microbiome as a set of 137 oral bacteria (only 7% of 1980 amplicon sequence variants) significantly influenced by social contact (quantified through wireless sensors of short-range interactions). We show that large interaction networks including strong links between close kin, spouses, and even unrelated friends, can significantly predict bacterial transmission networks across Agta camps. Finally, we show that more central individuals to social networks are also bacterial supersharers. We conclude that hunter-gatherer social microbiomes are predominantly pathogenic and were shaped by evolutionary tradeoffs between extensive sociality and disease spread.

papers.title_ja: R.K.ナラヤン、ムルク・ラジ・アナンド、ラジャ・ラオの作品における物語技法、テーマ、文化的表象の比較研究
papers.summary: ABSTRACT The paper gives a comparative literary discussion of R.K. Narayan, Mulk Raj Anand and Raja Rao- three pioneers of early Indian English literature. The paper will discuss their narrative styles, thematic interests, cultural depiction, and the contributions in general to the development of Indian writing in English. The researchers conclude that the narrative style of Narayan is characterised by simplicity, irony, and an interest in ordinary life, usually in the fictional town of Malgudi, which enables him to depict the middle-class Indian society in the form of subtle humour and humanism. Anand, on the contrary, is a socially engaged, realist who pre-empts problems like caste oppression, poverty, and colonial exploitation and thus speaks up on behalf of marginalised groups. Rao, in turn, combines philosophical questioning with mythical composition, using a more complex narrative device informed by Indian oral culture and spiritual philosophy. papers.title: Beyond the Dancefloor: Club Culture, Design and Nightlife
papers.title_ja: ダンスフロアを超えて：クラブカルチャー、デザイン、ナイトライフ
papers.summary: Beyond the Dance Floor offers the first critical inquiry into the relationship between design, club culture and broader international culture and creativity. Building on the editors’ pioneering work on the design and architecture history of nightclubs in the late 20th and early 21st centuries, this collection of new research will show the significant but under-recognized creativity of club culture and explore how its broader design-based interactions go beyond the dancefloor into the world outside the nightclub. Beyond the Dancefloor will assert the social, cultural, economic, and political, value of club culture by revealing its embeddedness in broader creative and cultural communities, industries and practices.
